To create a comprehensive test suite for the given requirements using Decision Tables, we need to define the conditions and actions for each requirement. Since the requirements are focused on the storage, management, and scalability of requirements in Doorstop, we will create decision tables that cover all possible scenarios.

### Decision Tables for Requirements

#### Decision Table for [REQ011]: Store requirements securely
| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Doorstop can store requirements | Store requirements securely |
| Doorstop cannot store requirements | Do not store requirements |

#### Decision Table for [REQ012]: Handle change management
| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Doorstop can handle change management | Handle change management |
| Doorstop cannot handle change management | Do not handle change management |

#### Decision Table for [REQ013]: Associate changes with developer identification
| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Doorstop can associate changes with developer identification | Associate changes with developer identification |
| Doorstop cannot associate changes with developer identification | Do not associate changes with developer identification |

#### Decision Table for [REQ014]: Scalability to support thousands of requirements
| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Doorstop supports scalability | Scalable to support thousands of requirements |
| Doorstop does not support scalability | Not scalable |

#### Decision Table for [REQ015]: Lightweight installation method
| Condition | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Doorstop has a lightweight installation method | Provide a lightweight installation method |
| Doorstop does not have a lightweight installation method | Do not provide a lightweight installation method |

This test suite covers all the requirements with positive test cases. For negative and boundary tests, additional scenarios would need to be defined based on the specific failure modes and edge cases for each requirement.
